result.title: EPRO: Robust Policy Optimization Through an Imperfect Execution-Policy Predictor
result.summary: RL for LLMs often separates rollout generation from policy training. Although the two numerical engines share model parameters, they can induce different policies. This creates a challenge beyond correcting a known training-inference mismatch: during learner updates, the execution policy corresponding to the current parameters cannot be directly observed. We view this as optimizing an unobserved execution policy through an imperfect predictor of its evolution. This perspective raises two fundamental questions: how can we estimate the execution policy's response to learner updates, and how much should we trust that estimate when optimizing the actual execution policy? We introduce Execution-Policy Robust Optimization (EPRO) to address these challenges. Starting from the observed rollout-time execution policy, we use training-policy changes to construct a differentiable predictor of the current execution policy, whose score yields Transported Score Centering (TSC). Our robust-improvement analysis reveals how prediction error limits the magnitude of reliably justified updates. For practical implementation, we introduce Policy Shift as an observable proxy for prediction risk and use Shift-Aware Soft Clipping (SSC) to attenuate risky updates. Across four Qwen3 model settings, EPRO achieves the highest average held-out accuracy among the compared methods on seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对 LLM 强化学习中 rollout 生成与训练所用策略不一致的问题，把训练时无法直接观测的「执行策略」视为需通过不完美预测器优化的对象，提出 EPRO：用训练策略变化构造可微预测器并给出 Transported Score Centering，同时以 Policy Shift 作为预测风险代理，用软裁剪衰减高风险更新，在多个 Qwen3 设置与数学推理基准上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「无法直接观测的状态只能由不完美预测器近似、并需按预测风险限制更新幅度」的思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态估计的可信度加权与训练信号贡献分配提供可核查的借鉴线索，但论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
